summary.en: María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela, sparking protests demanding elections and her continued presence. The United States has deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela while pressuring Reliance to refine Venezuelan oil, and CIA Director Ratcliffe visited Havana with a paramilitary operative linked to a past operation that killed 32 Cuban soldiers, indicating a shift in U.S. covert focus toward Cuba. The Pentagon has prohibited DoD personnel from using nonpublic information to bet on U.S. military actions involving Venezuela. UCDP counted 2 battle-related deaths in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: María Corina Machado har returnert til Venezuela, og har utløst protester som krever valg og hennes fortsatte tilstedeværelse. USA har satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer fra Space Force mot Venezuela, samtidig som de presser Reliance til å raffinere venezuelansk olje, og CIA-direktør Ratcliffe besøkte Havana med en paramilitær operativ knyttet til en tidligere operasjon som drepte 32 cubanske soldater, noe som indikerer et skifte i USAs hemmelige fokus mot Cuba. Pentagon har forbudt DoD-personell å bruke ikke-offentlig informasjon til å satse på amerikanske militære handlinger som involverer Venezuela. UCDP registrerte 2 dødsfall i kamp i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
